panels.rationale: Single coronal contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI of a real patient showing a heterogeneously enhancing pineal-region mass with markedly dilated lateral ventricles, consistent with the article's documented obstructive hydrocephalus due to aqueductal obstruction. The caption itself emphasizes the pineal mass, but the in-text description explicitly attributes the ventriculomegaly to obstructive hydrocephalus, supporting disease attribution at the figure level.
panels.attribution_text: Urquiza Portilla et al. Papillary Tumor of the Pineal Region Presenting With Obstructive Hydrocephalus: A Diagnostic and Management Challenge. Cureus None. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Preoperative coronal T1-weighted contrast-enhanced MRI of a pineal region mass. Contrast-enhanced coronal T1-weighted MRI revealing a heterogeneously enhancing mass in the pineal region (yellow arrow). The heterogeneous enhancement pattern and anatomic location raised initial concern for a pineal parenchymal tumor and prompted endoscopic third ventriculostomy with biopsy.
in_text_mentions: Non-contrast head CT demonstrated a pineal-region soft-tissue mass measuring approximately 15 × 12 mm, associated with third and lateral ventriculomegaly, mild transependymal CSF flow consistent with obstructive hydrocephalus, and mild cerebellar tonsillar crowding at the foramen magnum. Subsequent contrast-enhanced brain MRI confirmed a 13 × 12 × 13 mm lobulated, enhancing pineal lesion causing aqueductal obstruction (Figures 1-2); the initial radiologic differential diagnosis favored a pineal parenchymal tumor (pineocytoma).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial FLAIR MRI of a real patient showing dilated lateral and third ventricles with periventricular hyperintensity, the classic imaging manifestation of obstructive hydrocephalus as stated in the caption. B: Axial T2-weighted MRI of the same real patient demonstrating dilated lateral and third ventricles with periventricular transependymal oedema, a classic manifestation of obstructive hydrocephalus; arrow annotation present. C: Coronal T2-weighted MRI of a real patient showing hydrocephalic ventricular dilatation with an arrowed ectatic basilar artery compressing the third ventricle floor, an uncommon (variant) obstructive cause; the vascular finding is not in the provided vocabulary and is listed as a proposed finding.
